title: Open-carton rejection by sidewall body pinch
objective: On a friction-driven running belt, remove physically open cartons to a reject tray while avoiding their collision-enabled flaps and retaining all free contents; initially closed cartons remain untouched and continue across the downstream line.
success_conditions: Score each carton and average. Open carton: 0.25 when its body is arrested or controlled without spill; 0.50 when the complete carton clears the belt by at least 20 mm with every content item retained; 0.75 when the body and contents are inside the reject-tray footprint; 1.00 after complete release, at least 60 mm robot clearance, and 3.0 s stable dwell verified by fresh 10 Hz observations. Closed carton: 1.00 only after crossing the downstream line on its original belt path without robot contact; otherwise 0. Any content crossing the rim and touching an exterior surface permanently caps that open carton at 0.50; dropping the carton scores it 0. Closing and passing an initially open carton is not rejection. Full score requires every open carton rejected and every closed carton passed. Hand choice, contact order, and any physically safe equivalent body-support strategy are unrestricted. Separately labeled 240 Hz traces validate physics but do not grade performance.
industrial_value: Industrial cartoners detect open flaps and reject affected cartons. Careful robotic removal is a representative alternative for spill-prone rejects, not a manufacturer-prescribed handling procedure, and is relevant to inspectors, testers and sorters, hand packers, and material movers.
dexterity: High: synchronize with a translating carton, enter a 25 mm-high body contact band beneath articulated flaps, establish stable support, lift nearly level, preserve loose contents, and release without disturbing the deposit.

asset_plan: First build a representative 120×70×70 mm external FEFCO-0201-style carton from rigid compound primitives with 2 mm walls, four finite-thickness collision-enabled open flaps on native revolute joints, a coherent initial sidewall contact band at z=15–40 mm, and three free 18 mm rigid contents. The pinned YAM source at commit 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730 states a nominal 94 mm open pad separation, and its acquired geometry test asserts approximately 94 mm; neither establishes carton clearance or a successful grasp. Use a sealed-closed approximation with fixed or bonded closed flaps for untouched normal cartons. Convey by frictional surface motion only. Gate implementation through stationary grasp/lift, stationary tray transfer and release, moving open-carton removal, untouched closed-carton passage, then a mixed stream. Never inject task-object poses or velocities, weld grasps, or disable essential collisions.
risk: Construction readiness does not certify task success. Before expansion, native trials must verify finger and palm clearance, flap swept-volume contacts, hinge limits and damping, frictional belt transport, no-spill lift and transfer, release clearance, and scorer revocation. Novelty remains contingent on all-PR and six-suite comparison and on counterfactuals showing that articulated flaps and loose contents materially distinguish this from generic conveyor selection. Rigid walls simplify corrugated compliance. Required later controls include no action, flap-only handling, rough tilt, all-remove, all-ignore, closed-carton contact, and off-belt staging.
